solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unexpectedly bad issue is set right

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out of its normal order, so the letters of bad issue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor magazine edition has surprisingly been corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' rearranges BADISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from a mistaken belief is to correct them, putting them right about something.

clue.text: Drink from French restaurant that's inexpensive

parts.note: de is the French word for from
a caff is British slang for a cheap, basic café

explanation.surface: A beverage bought at a cheap French eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: A CAFF is the British informal word for a cheap café serving fry-ups and tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee with the caffeine removed is a common beverage ordered by that short name.

clue.text: Rising smells engulf area in autumn, say

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the first piece goes around the second
in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: noses are smells, as in a wine's nose

explanation.surface: Odours wafting upward fill the countryside in the fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns NOSES into SESON; 'engulf' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumn is one example of the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: Glitch involving mobile airship

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a blip is a minor glitch or temporary fault
M is a common abbreviation for mobile, as on a phone number list

explanation.surface: A technical fault affects a moving dirigible.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-rigid dirigible balloon is called by this name, so it is a kind of aircraft lighter than air.

clue.text: Abstract's reportedly like warm weather

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken or heard, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: summery means typical of the hot months of the year

explanation.surface: A statement that the abstract is said to resemble sunny days.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMMERY and the answer are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a short précis at the head of a paper, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Smear Duke involved in smooth enterprise initially

indicators.note: involved in places the duke inside the other word

parts.note: smug has an old sense of neat, sleek and smooth

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of enterprise

explanation.surface: A slur against an aristocrat mixed up in a slick business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge is a blurred mark, the same as a smear of ink or dirt.

clue.text: Absurd claim to be about chemical processes in the body

definitions.text: about chemical processes in the body
definitions.note: an adjective phrase, meaning concerning the body's chemistry

indicators.note: something absurd is nonsensical, so the letters of claim to be are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A ridiculous assertion about how the body works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absurd' rearranges CLAIMTOBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Metabolism is the set of chemical reactions in a living body, and this adjective means relating to it.

clue.text: Democrat angrily berates those who argue

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat in US politics

indicators.note: angrily suggests the letters of berates being thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A US politician furiously scolds people who disagree with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angrily' rearranges BERATES into EBATERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Debaters are people who argue formally for or against a motion.

clue.text: Converting a seedy hotel by the end of June will offer protection from the sun

indicators.note: converting a building remakes it, so these letters are refashioned into another order

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the end of picks the closing letter of June

explanation.surface: Renovating a run-down hotel by midsummer will give guests a shaded refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converting' rearranges ASEEDYH into EYESHAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor worn on the forehead shields the eyes from glare, so it protects against sunlight.

clue.text: It is a march. Or could be

definitions.note: it is informal for personal magnetism or allure

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of is a march might form another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about whether something is a parade or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ISAMARCH. 'It' as the definition means that special quality, as in 'she has it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having 'it' means possessing a compelling personal magnetism, exactly what charisma is.

clue.text: Lawman loses prisoner in outbuilding

indicators.note: loses means a part is dropped from the word

parts.note: a constable is a police officer
a con is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A police officer lets a convict escape in a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes CON from the start of CONSTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A building where horses are kept is a typical farm outhouse.

clue.text: Having died out deity mutates into mythical creature

indicators.note: mutates means changes form, so the remaining letters of deity are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A god, having become extinct, transforms into a legendary beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes D from DEITY, and 'mutates' rearranges the remaining EITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a creature of legend, never proven to exist.

clue.text: A lot of positive time and energy combined in stoker's station

indicators.note: combined means mixed together, so these letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Plenty of upbeat effort and hours are needed where the steam fireman works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combined' rearranges ALOTOF plus P, T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: On a steam locomotive the platform where driver and fireman stand is where the stoker shovels coal.

clue.text: Set piece of brick on church

parts.note: a bat is a broken piece of brick, as in brickbat

explanation.surface: A fragment of masonry is placed on a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch is a group of things made or dealt with together, a collection like a set.

clue.text: Sailor gets close to girl

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common term for a sailor
by means near or close to

explanation.surface: A seaman gets near a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of Abigail used as a female first name.

clue.text: I'll bet fibbers essentially did for fundamentalist Southern states

indicators.note: did for means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled
essentially means at the core, taking the central letters of fibbers

explanation.surface: A wager that liars brought about the downfall of the religious American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes BBE, the core of FIBBERS; 'did for' rearranges ILLBET plus BBE.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of the southern US where evangelical Protestant Christianity is strongest is known by this nickname.

clue.text: Rough non-unionist builder worked around Lough

indicators.note: around means the anagram wraps the other piece
worked means shaped or kneaded, so the remaining letters are rearranged
non means without, so the unionist letter is taken out

parts.note: U is an abbreviation for Unionist in UK politics
L is an abbreviation for lough, an Irish lake, on maps

explanation.surface: A coarse builder who refuses to join a union labours by an Irish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non' removes U from BUILDER, 'worked' rearranges BILDER into ILBRED, and 'around' puts L inside. A lough is an Irish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rough in manners is badly brought up, lacking courtesy and refinement.

clue.text: Wanderer in African country eaten by very active leopard in the end

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside the other piece

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for active, as in grammar

indicators.note: in the end picks the closing letter of leopard

parts.note: Gabon is a country in West Central Africa

explanation.surface: A traveller in Africa is devoured by a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten by' puts GABON inside V, A and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagabond is a homeless person who roams from place to place, a rover.

clue.text: For example the tops of her long legs could be thin and delicate

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: could be suggests these letters might be rearranged into something else
the tops of picks the first letters of her and long

explanation.surface: Remarking that a woman's upper thighs might be slender and fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the tops of' gives H and L; 'could be' rearranges HL plus LEGS into GSHELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective it describes china or a finish that is fragile and fine, like the brittle casing of an egg.

clue.text: Some elements briefly support a method of calculation

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
Ge is the chemical symbol for germanium
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A lab approach where a few chemical substances prop up a numerical technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some elements briefly' gives two chemical symbols, AL (aluminium) and GE (germanium).
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is the branch of mathematics that uses symbols for numbers to solve problems.

clue.text: American hero can be sarcastic

parts.note: El Cid was the Spanish national hero of the eleventh century

explanation.surface: A US action hero can be biting in his wit.
explanation.walkthrough: El CID is the legendary Spanish warrior hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid remarks are sharp and cutting, just as sarcastic ones are.

clue.text: Internal stitches irritate

indicators.note: internal means on the inside, so the answer is found within the word stitches

explanation.surface: Sutures beneath the skin cause irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: To prickle or be irritating is a verb sense, as in a woollen jumper that makes the skin tingle.

clue.text: Melting iron consumes new iron in huge fire

indicators.note: consumes means eats up, so the anagram takes the other letters inside it
melting changes a solid's shape, so the letters of iron flow into a new order

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Molten metal swallows fresh metal in a blazing furnace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Melting' rearranges the first 'iron' as IRNO; 'consumes' takes the other pieces inside it, the second 'iron' being its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a large, intense, out-of-control blaze.

clue.text: Warning about inclusion of Ecstasy in tax

parts.note: ca is the abbreviation for circa, meaning about

indicators.note: inclusion of means the drug letter is put inside the tax

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, a UK sales tax
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A caution regarding drugs being covered by a levy.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a cautionary proviso or qualification, a formal warning.

clue.text: More suitable for punter

definitions.meaning: comparative of good, meaning preferable or fitter

explanation.surface: A preferable option for a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of good means more fitting, and one who wagers is also a gambler, so both senses fit.

clue.text: I will broadcast in passageway

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the airwaves, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: I will contracts to I'll

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they will go on air from a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: I'LL is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats or shelves.

clue.text: Wearing mink, perhaps, one starts to antagonise the econuts leading to anger

parts.note: wearing clothes means being in them
mink is an example of an animal fur
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Wearing a mink coat is bound to provoke the green activists.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage someone is to make them furious, which is what anger means as a verb.

clue.text: Rascal's activity rises in street in Marseilles

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: rue is the French word for street

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: go means energy or activity

explanation.surface: A scoundrel's busy life goes up in a French city road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' works because this is a down clue: the word for activity is read upward before going into the French street.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous or dishonest person, the same as a scoundrel.

clue.text: Began to write in wordbook

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A writer started work on a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To start something, such as a meeting or a campaign, is to commence it.

clue.text: Fit lively German replacing one in bit part

indicators.note: lively means brisk and bustling, signalling the letters being stirred up
replacing means the word German is put where the single letter was

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sprightly German gets a small role in place of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' puts GERMAN where I is in FIT, giving FGERMANT; 'lively' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small piece broken off something, a bit or part.

clue.text: Cancel delegate's Parisian summer

parts.note: del. is an abbreviation for delegate
été is the French word for summer

explanation.surface: Calling off a representative's summer trip to Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete is to strike out or remove, as when cancelling an entry.

clue.text: Guide rope almost lasts out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A tether that nearly holds out acts as a guide for climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LASTS to LAST; 'out' rearranges ROPE plus LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the north star, has long guided navigators, so it is a figurative guiding principle.
